senses.def: a formal promise to tell the truth or to do something
ex: He took an oath to tell the truth.
The witness was under oath.

senses.def: the act of doing what you are told
ex: Dogs are trained to show obedience.
The army demands obedience.

senses.def: doing what you are told
ex: The dog was obedient.
She was an obedient child.

senses.def: to do what you are told or what a rule says
ex: Children must obey their parents.
Drivers should obey traffic laws.

mistake.note: Obey takes a direct object with no preposition.

senses.def: a thing that you can see and touch
ex: There was a strange object on the road.
She picked up a heavy object.

senses.def: a purpose or aim
ex: The object of the game is to score goals.
Money is no object.

senses.def: to say that you do not like or agree with something
ex: Many people objected to the plan.
I object to being called lazy.

senses.def: a reason or statement that shows you disagree with something
ex: Does anyone have an objection?
She raised an objection to the plan.

senses.def: something you plan to achieve
ex: Our objective is to win.
He met all his objectives.

senses.def: based on facts and not on personal opinions
ex: Judges must give an objective ruling.
Try to be objective about your work.

senses.def: something you must do because of a law or moral rule
ex: We have a moral obligation to help.
You are under no obligation to buy.

senses.def: to force someone to do something by law or duty
ex: The law obliges drivers to wear seat belts.
I felt obliged to help.

senses.def: to help someone by doing what they ask
ex: Could you oblige me with a pen?

senses.def: not stated directly
ex: He made an oblique reference to her mistake.
She gave an oblique answer.

senses.def: to make something difficult to see or understand
ex: Thick fog obscured the road.
Too much detail obscures the main point.

senses.def: not well known, or difficult to understand
ex: He wrote for an obscure magazine.
The meaning of the poem is obscure.

senses.def: the act of carefully watching someone or something
ex: The patient is under observation.
His observation of birds took years.

senses.def: a comment based on something you have noticed
ex: She made a clever observation about the book.

senses.def: to watch someone or something carefully
ex: Scientists observed the stars.
The nurse observed the patient.

senses.def: to say something that you have noticed
ex: He observed that the room was cold.

senses.def: to follow a rule or law
ex: You must observe the speed limit.

senses.def: a person who watches something happen
ex: International observers watched the vote.
She was a quiet observer.

senses.def: a thing that someone thinks about too much
ex: Football is his obsession.
Her obsession with clothes cost her a lot.

senses.def: thinking or worrying about something too much
ex: He is obsessive about cleaning.
She has an obsessive fear of germs.

senses.def: something that stops you from moving forward or succeeding
ex: Lack of money was a big obstacle.
The runners jumped over obstacles.

senses.def: to get something, especially through effort
ex: You need a visa to obtain a job there.
He obtained a copy of the report.

senses.def: easy to see or understand
ex: It was obvious that she was upset.
The answer is obvious.

senses.def: in a way that is easy to see or understand
ex: Obviously, I will help you.
He was obviously tired.

senses.def: a particular time when something happens
ex: I have met her on several occasions.
It was a special occasion.

senses.def: to cause something (formal)
ex: The delay occasioned great trouble.

senses.def: happening sometimes but not often
ex: I have an occasional coffee.
There will be occasional showers.

senses.def: sometimes, but not often
ex: We occasionally eat out.
He occasionally visits his aunt.

senses.def: connected with a person's job
ex: Back pain is an occupational hazard for nurses.
Occupational health services help workers.

senses.def: to be in a place and use it
ex: The family occupies the top floor.
Is this seat occupied?

senses.def: to take control of a place by force
ex: Soldiers occupied the town.
Protesters occupied the building.

senses.def: to keep someone's time or attention busy
ex: Reading occupied her afternoon.
The children kept themselves occupied.

senses.def: to happen, especially without being planned
ex: The accident occurred at night.
Earthquakes occur often in this region.

senses.def: to come into your mind (occur to someone)
ex: It never occurred to me to ask.
An idea occurred to her.

senses.def: a very large area of salt water
ex: They sailed across the Atlantic Ocean.
The ocean was calm.

senses.def: unusual or strange
ex: It's odd that she didn't call.
He has an odd sense of humour.

senses.def: an odd number cannot be divided exactly by two
ex: Three and five are odd numbers.

senses.def: used to show that something belongs to or is part of something
ex: The door of the car is red.
She is a friend of mine.

senses.def: used to show the contents or the amount of something
ex: I'd like a glass of water.
A group of children ran past.

mistake.note: Use 's with names and people; of is used mostly with things.

senses.def: not working or not switched on
ex: The lights are off.
The match is off because of rain.

senses.def: away from a place or position
ex: He drove off at speed.
She took her coat off.

senses.def: away from or down from something
ex: The cat jumped off the wall.
Keep off the grass.

senses.def: to make someone feel hurt or upset
ex: I hope I didn't offend you.
His comments offended many people.

senses.def: to commit a crime (offend)
ex: He offended again after leaving prison.

senses.def: a person who has committed a crime
ex: Young offenders go to special courts.
The offender was fined.

senses.def: an illegal act
ex: Parking here is an offence.
He was arrested for a serious offence.

senses.def: a feeling of being upset or insulted
ex: I meant no offence.
She took offence at his remarks.

senses.def: rude and likely to upset people
ex: The joke was offensive.
He used offensive language.

senses.def: used for attacking
ex: Offensive weapons are banned.

senses.def: something you say you will give or do for someone
ex: She accepted my offer of help.
They made me a good offer.

senses.def: to say that you will give or do something for someone
ex: He offered me a lift.
The shop offers free delivery.

mistake.note: After offer, use to + verb, or offer + person + thing.

senses.def: a room or building where people work at desks
ex: She works in a small office.
The office opens at nine.

senses.def: approved by an authority; formal
ex: The official language is Arabic.
She received an official letter.

senses.def: a person who has an important job in an organisation
ex: Government officials met yesterday.
A bank official answered my question.

senses.def: in a formal or approved way
ex: The bridge was officially opened in May.
He is officially the winner.

senses.def: at sea, not far from the coast
ex: They work on an offshore oil rig.
Offshore winds blow from the land.

senses.def: the young of people or animals
ex: The lion protects its offspring.
Her offspring are all at university.

senses.def: a thick liquid used as fuel or for cooking
ex: Fry the onions in olive oil.
The country exports oil.

senses.def: a soft cream that you put on the skin to heal it
ex: She put ointment on the burn.
The doctor gave me an ointment for my rash.

senses.def: acceptable or satisfactory
ex: The food was OK.
Is it OK if I open the window?

senses.def: in a satisfactory way
ex: He is doing OK at school.
The car runs OK.

senses.def: having lived or existed for a long time
ex: My grandfather is very old.
This is an old building.

mistake.note: Use a hyphen and no s in a five-year-old boy.

senses.def: not modern, or belonging to an earlier time
ex: She wears old-fashioned clothes.
It's an old-fashioned way to cook.

senses.def: a small green or black fruit with a bitter taste, eaten or pressed to make oil
ex: She added a few black olives to the salad.
Olive oil is common in Mediterranean cooking.

senses.def: touching and supported by a surface
ex: The keys are on the table.

senses.def: used before a day or date to say when something happens
ex: We have a meeting on Monday.

senses.def: about a subject
ex: He gave a talk on climate change.

senses.def: continuing without stopping
ex: She kept on walking.

senses.def: switched on and working
ex: Is the heating on?

mistake.wrong: I will see you in Monday.
mistake.right: I will see you on Monday.
mistake.note: Use on, not in, before days and dates.

senses.def: one time only
ex: I go to the gym once a week.

senses.def: at some time in the past
ex: He once lived in Cairo.

senses.def: as soon as something has happened
ex: Once you finish, call me.
Once she arrived, the meeting began.

senses.def: the number 1; a single
ex: I have one brother.

senses.def: the number 1
ex: One plus one is two.

senses.def: used instead of repeating a noun
ex: I lost my pen, so I bought a new one.

senses.def: any person, in formal speech
ex: One should always be polite.
One never knows what will happen.

senses.def: connected to or done using the internet
ex: She does her shopping with an online store.

senses.def: using the internet
ex: I booked the tickets online.

senses.def: being the one person or thing of a kind
ex: She is the only girl in the team.

senses.def: and nothing or no one else; just
ex: I only have ten pounds.

senses.def: no more than a small amount or time
ex: It only takes five minutes.

mistake.wrong: Only I can speak English here.
mistake.right: I can only speak English here.
mistake.note: Place only next to the word it limits, as the meaning changes with its position.

senses.def: moving to a position on a surface
ex: The cat jumped onto the sofa.
He stepped onto the stage.

mistake.wrong: The cat jumped on the sofa from the floor.
mistake.right: The cat jumped onto the sofa.
mistake.note: Use onto, not on, for movement towards a surface.

senses.def: not allowing light to pass through, so you cannot see through it
ex: The bathroom window is made of opaque glass.
Opaque tights hide the skin completely.

senses.def: difficult to understand or explain clearly
ex: The rules of the contract were opaque.
The company's opaque decisions upset staff.

senses.def: not closed, so people or things can go in or out
ex: The window is open.

senses.def: ready for customers or people to enter
ex: The shop is open until nine.

senses.def: honest and not hiding your feelings or thoughts
ex: She is open about her problems.

senses.def: to move something so that it is no longer closed
ex: Please open the door.

senses.def: to start business or begin an event
ex: The new bank opens on Friday.

senses.def: a hole or space that something can go through
ex: There is an opening in the fence.

senses.def: the beginning of something, or the first part of it
ex: The opening of the film is very funny.
We went to the opening of a new museum.

senses.def: a job that is available
ex: The firm has an opening for a designer.

senses.def: in an honest way, without hiding anything
ex: He spoke openly about his illness.
They openly disagree with the plan.

senses.def: medical treatment in which a doctor cuts into the body
ex: He had an operation on his knee.

senses.def: an organised activity involving many people
ex: The police began a rescue operation.
The operation took two weeks.

senses.def: the way that a machine or system works
ex: The operation of the machine is simple.
The factory is now in operation.

senses.def: a person whose job is to use a machine or piece of equipment
ex: The crane operator saw the problem.
A skilled operator can fix this machine.

senses.def: a person who connects phone calls
ex: Ask the operator for the number.
I spoke to a phone operator.

senses.def: a company that runs a service
ex: The tour operator cancelled the trip.
Rail operators raised their prices.

senses.def: a thought or belief about something or someone
ex: In my opinion, uniforms are a good idea.
What's your opinion of the new manager?

mistake.right: In my opinion, ... / In my view, ...
mistake.note: Use according to for other people's opinions or sources, never for your own.

senses.def: a person you play or compete against
ex: She beat her opponent in two sets.
The team has a strong opponent today.

senses.def: a person who disagrees with an idea or plan
ex: Opponents of the plan held a protest.
He is a strong opponent of the law.

senses.def: a chance to do something good or useful
ex: I had an opportunity to travel abroad.
This is a great opportunity for you.

mistake.wrong: I have a good opportunity of studying abroad.
mistake.right: I have a good opportunity to study abroad.
mistake.note: Say opportunity to do something, or opportunity for something, not opportunity of.

senses.def: on the other side, facing something
ex: She lives on the opposite side of the street.

senses.def: completely different in direction or meaning
ex: They walked in opposite directions.

senses.def: on the other side of something and facing it
ex: The bank is opposite the station.

senses.def: in a position facing someone or something
ex: They live in the house opposite.

senses.def: a person or thing that is as different as possible from another
ex: Hot is the opposite of cold.
He is the opposite of his brother.

senses.def: strong disagreement with a plan or idea
ex: There was strong opposition to the new road.

senses.def: the political parties that are not in government
ex: The opposition criticised the budget.
Opposition leaders met on Friday.

senses.def: the feeling that good things will happen
ex: She spoke with great optimism about the future.
There is optimism about the economy.

senses.def: expecting good things to happen
ex: I'm optimistic about my chances of winning.
He gave an optimistic forecast.

senses.def: something that you can choose
ex: You have two options: stay or leave.
Taking the train is a cheap option.

senses.def: a subject that students can choose to study
ex: Art is an option in the second year.

senses.def: looking very expensive and rich
ex: They stayed in an opulent hotel.
The palace had opulent rooms full of gold.

senses.def: used between choices or possibilities
ex: Do you want tea or coffee?

senses.def: used to say what will happen if something is not done
ex: Hurry up, or we will miss the bus.

senses.def: a test in which you speak your answers
ex: I have my English oral tomorrow.

senses.def: spoken, not written
ex: There will be an oral test.
She gave an oral report.

senses.def: of or taken through the mouth
ex: Oral medicine is easy to take.
Good oral health starts with brushing.

senses.def: the curved path of an object around a planet or star
ex: The satellite is in orbit around Earth.
The moon's orbit takes about a month.

senses.def: a piece of land where fruit trees are grown
ex: They own an apple orchard near the village.
We picked cherries in the orchard.

senses.def: a large group of musicians who play together
ex: She plays the violin in the city orchestra.

senses.def: played by or written for an orchestra
ex: We listened to an orchestral concert.
He writes orchestral music for films.

senses.def: a plant with unusual, brightly coloured flowers
ex: She keeps a white orchid in her kitchen.
Orchids grow well in warm, wet places.

senses.def: a request for food or goods
ex: The waiter took our order.

senses.def: the way things are arranged one after another
ex: Put the names in alphabetical order.

senses.def: something that someone in power tells you to do
ex: The soldiers followed their orders.
The judge gave an order to stop.

senses.def: to ask for food or goods to be brought or sent
ex: I ordered a pizza online.

senses.def: to tell someone to do something
ex: The officer ordered them to leave.

mistake.note: After order someone, use to plus the base verb.

senses.def: neatly arranged or well organised
ex: Her desk is always orderly.

senses.def: behaving in a calm and controlled way
ex: The crowd made an orderly line.

senses.def: in most cases; usually
ex: Ordinarily, I walk to work.
Ordinarily he wouldn't say such a thing.

senses.def: not special or different in any way
ex: It was an ordinary day at school.
She is just an ordinary person.

senses.def: rock from which metal is taken
ex: The mine produces iron ore.
Workers load the ore onto trucks.

senses.def: a part of the body with a particular job, such as the heart
ex: The liver is a vital organ.

senses.def: a large musical instrument with keys and pipes, often in a church
ex: The organ played during the wedding.

senses.def: produced without using artificial chemicals
ex: We buy organic vegetables at the market.

senses.def: from or relating to living things
ex: Organic waste can become compost.

senses.def: a group of people working together for a purpose
ex: She works for a charity organization.

senses.def: the act of arranging or planning something
ex: The organization of the event took months.
Good organization saves time.

senses.def: the place or point where something begins
ex: The origin of the word is Latin.

senses.def: the country, family or social group someone comes from
ex: He is of Egyptian origin.
People of all origins live here.

senses.def: existing at the beginning, before any changes
ex: The original door is still in the house.

senses.def: new and different from anything before
ex: She has some very original ideas.
The film has an original story.

senses.def: the first version of something, not a copy
ex: Keep the original and give them a copy.
The painting in the museum is an original.

senses.def: at the beginning, before any change
ex: The house was originally a school.
I'm originally from Jordan.

senses.def: covered with a lot of detailed decoration
ex: The ceiling is ornate and covered with gold.
She sat on an ornate chair.

senses.def: seeming to be true but possibly not the real reason
ex: He went to Paris ostensibly for work.
Ostensibly, the meeting was about safety.

senses.def: used for additional or different people or things
ex: Do you have any other questions?

senses.def: the second of two things
ex: Hold it in your other hand.

senses.def: a different person or thing
ex: One bag is red and the other is blue.

mistake.wrong: I have two sisters. One is a doctor and another is a teacher.
mistake.right: I have two sisters. One is a doctor and the other is a teacher.
mistake.note: Use the other for the last of two, and another for one more of many.

senses.def: used to say what would happen if something were different
ex: Take a coat, otherwise you'll be cold.

senses.def: in other ways, apart from what was just mentioned
ex: The room was cold but otherwise fine.
He was otherwise a good student.

senses.def: a small furry animal that swims well and eats fish
ex: We saw an otter in the river.
Otters often play in the water.

senses.def: a unit of weight equal to about 28 grams
ex: Add two ounces of butter.
The baby weighed ten ounces less.

senses.def: belonging to or connected with the speaker and others
ex: Our house is near the sea.

senses.def: used when we do something and it affects us
ex: We enjoyed ourselves at the party.

senses.def: used to stress that we did something without help
ex: We painted the room ourselves.

senses.def: away from the inside of a place
ex: She ran out of the house.

senses.def: not at home or at work
ex: Mum is out this afternoon.

senses.def: the sudden start of something bad, such as a disease or war
ex: There was an outbreak of flu at school.
The outbreak of war surprised everyone.

senses.def: the final result of an event or process
ex: We are happy with the outcome of the talks.
The outcome of the vote is not clear.

senses.def: on the outside; furthest from the centre
ex: The outer wall is made of stone.

senses.def: a set of clothes worn together
ex: She bought a new outfit for the wedding.
He wore a bright orange outfit.

senses.def: a short trip for pleasure
ex: We went on a family outing to the zoo.
The school outing was great fun.

senses.def: a shop or place that sells goods of one company
ex: The brand has outlets in every city.
We bought shoes at a factory outlet.

senses.def: a way of expressing feelings or energy
ex: Painting is a good outlet for stress.
Sport gives children an outlet for energy.

senses.def: the amount of something that a person or machine produces
ex: The factory's output rose by ten per cent.
Oil output has fallen this year.

senses.def: a strong feeling of anger and shock
ex: The decision caused public outrage.
She felt outrage at the unfair treatment.

senses.def: so unfair or bad that it makes you angry
ex: The price of the ticket is outrageous.
It was outrageous behaviour.

senses.def: not in a building; in the open air
ex: The children are playing outside.

senses.def: not in or inside a place
ex: She waited outside the school.

senses.def: on the outer part of something
ex: Paint the outside wall white.
The outside temperature is low.

senses.def: the outer part or surface of something
ex: The outside of the house is dirty.
From the outside, it looks small.

senses.def: a person who does not belong to a group
ex: As a new student, she felt like an outsider.
The club does not accept outsiders.

senses.def: the areas around the edge of a town or city
ex: They live on the outskirts of Riyadh.
The airport is on the outskirts of the city.

senses.def: extremely good or impressive
ex: She won a prize for outstanding work.

senses.def: not yet paid or dealt with
ex: He still has outstanding bills.
Several issues are still outstanding.

senses.def: shaped like an egg or a stretched circle
ex: We sat at an oval table.
She has an oval face.

senses.def: above or higher than something
ex: A lamp hung over the table.

senses.def: more than a number or amount
ex: The room holds over fifty people.

senses.def: from one side of something to the other
ex: He jumped over the wall.

senses.def: finished or ended
ex: The lesson is over.

senses.def: from standing to lying position
ex: The glass fell over.

senses.def: including everything or everyone
ex: The overall cost was higher than planned.
He gave an overall view of the project.

senses.def: taking everything into account
ex: Overall, the trip was a success.
Overall, prices have risen.

senses.def: a piece of clothing that covers the body, worn to protect clothes at work
ex: The painter wore white overalls.
Workers must put on overalls in the factory.

senses.def: over the side of a boat into the water
ex: He fell overboard during the storm.
A wave threw the bag overboard.

senses.def: to succeed in dealing with a problem or fear
ex: She overcame her fear of flying.

senses.def: to be strongly affected by a feeling or by smoke
ex: He was overcome with joy.
Smoke overcame several people.

senses.def: to lay or place something on top of something else
ex: The map is overlaid with a grid.
They overlay the photo with text.

senses.def: to have a view of something from above
ex: Our room overlooks the sea.
The hotel overlooks a large park.

senses.def: to fail to see or think about something
ex: I overlooked one mistake in the report.
Don't overlook the small details.

senses.def: to a greater degree than is good
ex: He was not overly worried about the test.
She is overly polite.

senses.def: lasting or happening through the night
ex: We took an overnight train to Cairo.

senses.def: sudden and complete
ex: The singer became an overnight success.

senses.def: for or during the night
ex: They stayed overnight at a friend's house.

senses.def: very quickly or suddenly
ex: Things did not change overnight.

senses.def: to watch work to make sure it is done correctly
ex: She oversees a team of ten.
A manager oversees all the building work.

senses.def: to remove a leader or government by force
ex: The army overthrew the government.
They tried to overthrow the king.

senses.def: in addition to normal working hours
ex: She works overtime on Fridays.
They worked overtime to finish.

senses.def: time worked in addition to normal hours, or the money paid for it
ex: He gets paid extra for overtime.
There is a lot of overtime this month.

senses.def: very strong or large, and hard to deal with
ex: She felt an overwhelming sadness.

senses.def: very large in number or amount
ex: The overwhelming majority voted yes.
There was overwhelming support.

senses.def: a word said when you feel sudden pain
ex: Ow! That hurt!
'Ow!' he cried, hitting his thumb.

senses.def: to have to pay money back to someone
ex: I owe my brother ten pounds.

senses.def: to have something because of someone or something
ex: She owes her success to hard work.
We owe you an explanation.

mistake.note: Owe takes the person first and the thing second, without to.

senses.def: a bird with large eyes that hunts at night
ex: We heard an owl in the garden.
Owls can see well in the dark.

senses.def: belonging to you and not to anyone else
ex: She has her own room.

senses.def: belonging to a person, not to others
ex: I don't borrow cars; I have my own.

senses.def: to have something that belongs to you
ex: He owns two shops in town.

mistake.wrong: This is my own car, not of my father.
mistake.right: This is my own car, not my father's.
mistake.note: Own follows a possessive such as my, his or the company's, never an article.

senses.def: a large male cow used for farm work
ex: The farmer used an ox to pull the plough.
Oxen pulled the heavy cart.

senses.def: a gas in the air that people need to breathe
ex: Plants give out oxygen.
